readings.title: Judgment on Moab and Ammon
readings.subtitle: Their reproach against God's people will be punished.
readings.text: [Zephaniah 2:8] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have heard <dn>את</dn> the reproach of Mo’aḇ, and <dn>את</dn> the revilings of the children of Ammon, with which they have reproached <dn>My</dn> people, and exalted themselves against their borders.</dq> [9] <dq>“Therefore, as <dn>I</dn> live,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>“Mo’aḇ shall be like Seḏom, and the children of Ammon like Amorah – a possession for weeds and a pit of salt, and a waste forever, the remnant of <dn>My</dn> people plunder them, and the rest of <dn>My</dn> nation possess them.”</dq> [10] This is what they get for their pride, because they have reproached and exalted themselves against the people of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts. [11] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall be awesome to them, for <dn>He</dn> shall make <dn>את</dn> all the mighty ones of the earth to shrivel, while all the coastlands of the nations bow down to <dn>Him</dn>, each one from his place.

readings.title: Judgment on Kush and Assyria
readings.subtitle: Nineveh will become a desolate ruin.
readings.text: [Zephaniah 2:12] <dq>“You too, O Kushites, are to be slain by <dn>My</dn> sword.”</dq> [13] And <dn>He</dn> shall stretch out <dn>His</dn> hand against the north, and destroy <dn>את</dn> Ashshur, and make <dn>את</dn> Ninevěh a waste, as dry as a wilderness. [14] And droves shall lie down in her midst, every beast of the nation, both pelican and bittern lodge in the tops of her columns, a voice singing at the window, ruin be at the threshold, for the cedar work is exposed. [15] This is the exultant city that is dwelling in safety, that said in her heart, “I am it, and there is none but me.” How has she become a waste, a place for beasts to lie down! Everyone who passes by her whistles and shakes his fist.

readings.subsection: The Corrupt City and Its Redemption
readings.title: Woe to Rebellious Jerusalem
readings.subtitle: The city has rejected instruction and corrupted its ways.
readings.text: [Zephaniah 3:1] Woe to her who is rebellious and defiled, the oppressing city! [2] She did not obey the voice, she did not accept <dn>את</dn> instruction, she did not trust in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, she did not draw near to her <dn>Elohim</dn>. [3] Her rulers in her midst are roaring lions, her judges are evening wolves, they shall leave no bone until morning. [4] Her prophets are reckless, treacherous men. Her priests have profaned <dn>את</dn> the set-apart place, they have done violence to the Torah. [5] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is righteous in her midst, <dn>He</dn> does no unrighteousness. Morning by morning <dn>He</dn> brings <dn>His</dn> right-ruling to light, it has not been lacking, yet the unrighteous one knows no shame. [6] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have cut off nations, their corner towers are in ruins. <dn>I</dn> have made their streets deserted, with no one passing by. Their cities are destroyed, without man, without inhabitant.</dq> [7] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have said, ‘Only fear <dn>Me</dn>, accept instruction.’ And her dwelling would not be cut off, all that <dn>I</dn> have appointed for her. But they rose up early, they corrupted all their deeds.</dq>

readings.subsection: The Corrupt City and Its Redemption
readings.title: A Purified Remnant
readings.subtitle: The humble will trust in the Name of YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [Zephaniah 3:8] <dq>“Therefore wait for <dn>Me</dn>,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“until the day <dn>I</dn> rise up for plunder. For <dn>My</dn> judgment is to gather nations, to assemble reigns, to pour out on them <dn>My</dn> rage, all <dn>My</dn> burning wrath. For by the fire of <dn>My</dn> jealousy all the earth shall be consumed.</dq> [9] <dq>“For then <dn>I</dn> shall turn unto the peoples a clean lip, so that they all call on the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to serve <dn>Him</dn> with one shoulder.</dq> [10] <dq>“From beyond the rivers of Kush my worshippers, the daughter of <dn>My</dn> dispersed ones, shall bring <dn>My</dn> offering.</dq> [11] <dq>“In that day you shall not be put to shame for any of your deeds in which you have transgressed against <dn>Me</dn>, for then <dn>I</dn> shall remove from your midst your proud exulting ones, and you shall no more be haughty in <dn>My</dn> set-apart mountain.</dq> [12] <dq>“But <dn>I</dn> shall leave in your midst an oppressed and poor people, and they shall trust in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [13] <dq>“The remnant of Yisra’ěl shall do no unrighteousness and speak no falsehood, nor is a tongue of deceit found in their mouth. For they shall feed their flocks and lie down, with none to frighten them.”</dq>

readings.subsection: The Corrupt City and Its Redemption
readings.title: A Song of Joy for Zion
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH will rejoice over His redeemed people.
readings.text: [Zephaniah 3:14] Shout for joy, O daughter of Tsiyon! Shout, O Yisra’ěl! Be glad and rejoice with all your heart, O daughter of Yerushalayim! [15] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has turned aside your judgments. <dn>He</dn> has faced your enemy. The Sovereign of Yisra’ěl, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, is in your midst. No longer need you fear <dn>את</dn> evil. [16] In that day it shall be said to Yerushalayim, “Do not fear, Tsiyon, do not let your hands be weak. [17] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> in your midst, is mighty to save. <dn>He</dn> rejoices over you with joy, <dn>He</dn> is silent in <dn>His</dn> love, <dn>He</dn> rejoices over you with singing.” [18] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall gather those who grieve about the appointed time, who are among you, to whom its reproach is a burden.</dq> [19] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am dealing with <dn>את</dn> all those afflicting you at that time. And <dn>I</dn> shall save <dn>את</dn> the lame, and gather those who were cast out. And <dn>I</dn> shall give them for a praise and for a name in all the earth where they were put to shame.</dq> [20] <dq>“At that time <dn>I</dn> shall bring you in, even at the time <dn>I</dn> gather you, for <dn>I</dn> shall give you for a name, and for a praise, among all the peoples of the earth, when <dn>I</dn> turn back your captivity before your eyes,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Death of King Josiah
readings.subtitle: Pharaoh Necho kills Josiah at Megiddo.
readings.text: [2 Kings 23:29] In his days Pharaoh Neḵo sovereign of Mitsrayim went up against the sovereign of Ashshur, to the River Euphrates. And Sovereign Yoshiyahu went out to him, and he killed him at Meḡiddo when he saw him. [30] And his servants conveyed <dn>את</dn> his body in a chariot from Meḡiddo, and brought him to Yerushalayim, and buried him in his own burial-place. And the people of the land took <dn>את</dn> Yeho’aḥaz son of Yoshiyahu, and anointed him, and set him up to reign in his father’s place.

readings.title: Prophecy Against the Philistines
readings.subtitle: The sword of YeHoVaH is appointed against Ashkelon.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 47:1] The word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> that came to Yirmeyahu the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck <dn>את</dn> Azzah: [2] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“See, waters are rising out of the north, and shall be an overflowing flood. And they shall overflow the land and all that is in it, the city and those who dwell within. And men shall cry, and all the inhabitants of the land shall wail.</dq> [3] <dq>“At the noise of the stamping hooves of his strong horses, at the rushing of his chariots, at the rumbling of his wheels, the fathers shall not look to their children, because of weakness of hands,</dq> [4] <dq>because of the day that shall come to ravage all the Philistines, to cut off from Tsor and Tsiḏon every helper that survives. For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is ravaging the Philistines, the remnant of the isle of Kaphtor.</dq> [5] <dq>“Baldness shall come upon Azzah, Ashqelon shall be cut off with the remnant of their valley. Till when would you cut yourself?</dq> [6] <dq>“O you sword of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, how long till you rest? Put yourself up into your sheath, rest and be still!</dq> [7] <dq>“How shall it rest, when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given it a command? Against Ashqelon and against the seashore – there <dn>He</dn> has appointed it.”</dq>

readings.title: Judgment on Moab
readings.subtitle: Woe to Nebo, for Moab is ravaged.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 48:1] Concerning Mo’aḇ. This is what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl said, <dq>“Woe to Neḇo! For it is ravaged, Qiryathayim is put to shame, captured. The high stronghold is put to shame and broken down.</dq> [2] <dq>“There is praise for Mo’aḇ no longer. In Ḥeshbon they have devised evil against her, ‘Come and let us cut it off as a nation.’ O Maḏměn, you are also cut off, a sword goes after you.</dq> [3] <dq>“Listen! An outcry from Ḥoronayim, ravaging and great destruction!</dq> [4] <dq>“Mo’aḇ shall be destroyed, her little ones shall cry out.</dq> [5] <dq>“For on the ascent to Luḥith they go up weeping bitterly. For in the descent of Ḥoronayim the enemies shall hear a cry of destruction.</dq> [6] <dq>“Flee, deliver your own lives! And be like a bush in the wilderness.</dq> [7] <dq>“For because you have trusted in your works and your treasures, you shall be captured. And Kemosh shall go forth into exile, his priests and his heads together.</dq> [8] <dq>“And a ravager shall come into every city, no one escapes. And the valley shall perish, and the plain be destroyed, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken.</dq> [9] <dq>“Give wings to Mo’aḇ, for she has to flee away, and her cities become a ruin, with no one to dwell in them.”</dq> [10] (Cursed is he who is slack in doing the work of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and cursed is he who withholds his sword from blood).

readings.title: Moab's Complacency Judged
readings.subtitle: The strong scepter has been broken.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 48:11] <dq>“Mo’aḇ has been at ease from his youth, and he has settled on his dregs, and has not been emptied from vessel to vessel, nor has he gone into exile. Therefore his flavour has stayed in him, and his fragrance is unchanged.</dq> [12] <dq>“Therefore see, the days are coming,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“when <dn>I</dn> shall send him tilters, who shall tilt him over and empty his vessels and break the bottles.</dq> [13] <dq>“And Mo’aḇ shall be ashamed because of Kemosh, as the house of Yisra’ěl was ashamed of Běyth Ěl, their refuge.</dq> [14] <dq>“How do you say, ‘We are mighty and strong men for battle’?</dq> [15] <dq>“Mo’aḇ is ravaged and her cities have been entered. And her chosen young men have gone down to the slaughter,”</dq> declares the Sovereign, whose Name is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts. [16] <dq>“The calamity of Mo’aḇ is near to come and his affliction hurries fast.</dq> [17] <dq>“Lament for him, all you who are around him. And all you who know his name, say, ‘How the strong sceptre has been broken, the staff of splendour!’</dq> [18] <dq>"Come down from your esteem, and sit in thirst, O inhabitant, daughter of Diḇon. For the ravager of Mo’aḇ shall come against you, he shall destroy your strongholds.</dq> [19] <dq>“Stand by the way and watch, O inhabitant of Aro‛ěr. Ask him who flees and her who escapes; say, ‘What has been done?’</dq> [20] <dq>“Mo’aḇ has been put to shame, for it has been broken down. Howl and cry! Let it be heard in Arnon that Mo’aḇ is ravaged.</dq>

readings.title: Judgment on Moab's Cities
readings.subtitle: The horn of Moab is cut off for its pride.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 48:21] <dq>“And judgment has come on the plain country, on Ḥolon and on Yaḥtsah and on Mopha‛ath,</dq> [22] <dq>and on Diḇon and Neḇo and on Běyth Diḇlathayim,</dq> [23] <dq>and on Qiryathayim and on Běyth Gamul and on Běyth Me‛on,</dq> [24] <dq>and on Qeriyoth and on Botsrah, and on all the cities of the land of Mo’aḇ, far or near.</dq> [25] <dq>“The horn of Mo’aḇ has been cut off, and his arm has been broken,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [26] <dq>“Make him drunk, because he has made himself great against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Mo’aḇ shall splash in his vomit, and he shall also be in mockery.</dq> [27] <dq>“And was not Yisra’ěl a mockery to you? Was he found among thieves? For whenever you speak of him, you shake your head.</dq> [28] <dq>“O inhabitants of Mo’aḇ, leave the cities and dwell in the rock, and be like the dove making a nest in the sides of the cave’s mouth.</dq> [29] <dq>“We have heard of the pride of Mo’aḇ (he is very proud!), of his loftiness and arrogance and pride, and of the haughtiness of his heart.”</dq> [30] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> know his wrath,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“and his boastings are untrue, and his deeds are false.</dq>

readings.title: A Lament for Moab
readings.subtitle: Joy and gladness are taken from the land.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 48:31] <dq>“Therefore <dn>I</dn> wail for Mo’aḇ, and <dn>I</dn> cry out for all Mo’aḇ. <dn>I</dn> mourn for the men of Qir Ḥeres.</dq> [32] <dq>“O vine of Siḇmah! <dn>I</dn> weep for you with the weeping of Ya‛zěr. Your branches have passed over the sea, they have come to the sea of Ya‛zěr. The ravager has fallen on your summer fruit and your grape harvest.</dq> [33] <dq>“Joy and gladness have been taken away from the orchard and from the land of Mo’aḇ. And <dn>I</dn> have made wine to cease from the winepresses. No one treads with shouting – the shouting is no shouting!</dq> [34] <dq>“From the outcry of Ḥeshbon unto El‛alěh, unto Yahats, they shall raise their voice, from Tso‛ar to Ḥoronayim, like a three-year-old heifer, for even the waters of Nimrim are dried up.</dq> [35] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall make an end in Mo’aḇ to him who offers in the high places and burns incense to his mighty ones,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [36] <dq>“So <dn>My</dn> heart sounds for Mo’aḇ like flutes, and <dn>My</dn> heart sounds for the men of Qir Ḥeres like flutes. Therefore the wealth they made shall be gone.</dq> [37] <dq>“For every head is bald, and every beard clipped – cuts on all the hands, and sackcloth on the loins.</dq> [38] <dq>“On all the house-tops of Mo’aḇ and in its streets it is all lamentation, for <dn>I</dn> have broken Mo’aḇ like a vessel in which no one delights,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [39] <dq>“How has she been broken down! They shall wail! How has Mo’aḇ turned her back with shame! So Mo’aḇ shall be a mockery and a horror to all those about her.”</dq>

readings.title: Moab's Final Destruction and Future Hope
readings.subtitle: Their captivity will be turned back in the latter days.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 48:40] For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“See, he soars like an eagle, and shall spread his wings over Mo’aḇ.</dq> [41] <dq>“Qeriyoth shall be captured, and the strongholds seized. And the heart of the mighty men in Mo’aḇ on that day shall be like the heart of a woman in labour.</dq> [42] <dq>“And Mo’aḇ shall be destroyed as a people, because he has made himself great against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [43] <dq>“Fear and the pit and the snare are upon you, O inhabitant of Mo’aḇ,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [44] <dq>“He who flees from the fear falls into the pit, and he who gets out of the pit is caught in the snare. For <dn>I</dn> am bringing upon Mo’aḇ the year of their punishment,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [45] <dq>“Those who fled stood powerless under the shadow of Ḥeshbon. But a fire shall come out of Ḥeshbon, and a flame from the midst of Siḥon, and consume the brow of Mo’aḇ and the crown of the head of the sons of uproar.</dq> [46] <dq>“Woe to you, O Mo’aḇ! The people of Kemosh have perished, for your sons have been taken into exile, and your daughters into exile.</dq> [47] <dq>“But <dn>I</dn> shall turn back the captivity of Mo’aḇ in the latter days,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Thus far is the judgment of Mo’aḇ.
